title: BPL Best Practices
description: Write professional-quality BPL code. Learn coding standards, documentation, testing approaches, and performance tips.

sections.title: Code Style and Naming
sections.content:
**Consistent naming makes code readable:**

| Element | Convention | Example |
|---------|------------|----------|
| Types/Structs | PascalCase | `HttpRequest`, `UserProfile` |
| Functions | camelCase | `getUserById`, `calculateTotal` |
| Variables | camelCase | `userName`, `itemCount` |
| Constants | SCREAMING_CASE | `MAX_BUFFER_SIZE`, `PI` |
| Files | snake_case | `user_service.bpl`, `http_client.bpl` |

**Formatting:**
- 4 spaces for indentation (no tabs)
- Braces on same line
- Space after keywords: `if (`, `loop (`
- No trailing whitespace

sections.title: Documentation Guidelines
sections.content:
**Comment the WHY, not the WHAT:**

```bpl
# ❌ BAD: Restates the code
local x: int = 5;  # Set x to 5

# ✅ GOOD: Explains intent
local retryCount: int = 5;  # Max retries before giving up
```

**Document complex functions:**

```bpl
# Calculates shipping cost based on weight and distance.
# 
# Parameters:
#   weightKg - Package weight in kilograms
#   distanceKm - Shipping distance in kilometers
# 
# Returns: Shipping cost in cents
# 
# Note: Minimum charge is 500 cents ($5)
frame calculateShipping(weightKg: float, distanceKm: int) ret int {
    ...
}
```

sections.title: Code Review Checklist
sections.content:
Before submitting code, verify:

**Correctness:**
- [ ] All edge cases handled
- [ ] Error paths tested
- [ ] No memory leaks
- [ ] No undefined behavior

**Readability:**
- [ ] Clear naming
- [ ] Functions under 30 lines
- [ ] Complex logic documented
- [ ] Consistent formatting

**Robustness:**
- [ ] Input validation
- [ ] Null checks where needed
- [ ] Bounds checking
- [ ] Proper cleanup (defer)

**Performance:**
- [ ] No unnecessary allocations
- [ ] Appropriate data structures
- [ ] No O(n²) when O(n) possible

sections.title: Practice: Refactor Bad Code
sections.hint: Better name: findIndex. Return Maybe<int> instead of -1. Document what it does.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.content:
✅ **Name clearly** - PascalCase types, camelCase functions/vars

✅ **Single responsibility** - each function does one thing

✅ **Return early** - check errors first, happy path flows

✅ **Use Result/Option** - explicit error handling

✅ **Document WHY** - not what the code does

✅ **Prefer stack** - faster, automatic cleanup

✅ **Review before commit** - use the checklist

questions.question: Which naming convention is correct for a BPL struct?
questions.explanation: Structs and types use PascalCase in BPL.

questions.question: What should comments explain?
questions.explanation: Comments should explain WHY, not WHAT - the code shows what it does.

questions.question: When should you prefer stack over heap allocation?
options: When size is known and small
questions.explanation: Use stack when size is known at compile time and reasonable - it's faster with automatic cleanup.
